DestReuseBinary at 16-bit DEST (fp32_dest_acc_en=False, DEST_AUTO_LIMIT=8): block_size==8 CORRUPTS rows 16-31 of the LAST tile of every DEST block (pcc 0.983 vs 0.99998). block_size<=7 exact. At fp32 DEST (limit 4) block==limit is fine. The chain clamps block_size to DEST_AUTO_LIMIT but a DestReuse chain needs one slot of headroom at 16-bit DEST -> missing static_assert/clamp in chain_max_block_v.

bank-major stateful REGRESSES bandwidth-bound regimes: dram_bound(64 cores) rd_only 42420->49607 (+17%), wide 295887->405266 (+37%), fp32 wr_only 12008->17639 (+47%). Cause: bank-major order makes every core hammer one DRAM channel at a time (all cores start at page%8==0). Order-preserving variants one_packet/affine give -13/-15% on focus with no reordering. bf8b (1088B pages) WINS big with bank_state: 12131->7473 copy (-38%). VERDICT WIN (modest, universal) for order-preserving one_packet/affine: focus rd_only 8090->6980 (-13.7%), wr_only 8609->7293 (-15.3%), copy 12462->10655 (-14.5%). Flat on dram_bound/wide/rm/fp32 (bandwidth-bound). one_packet has no B0 regression (tiny 724->701); affine costs +9% at 1 page (bank-table build). Stateful bank-major (B13 proper) REGRESSES bandwidth-bound regimes (+17/+37/+47%) but WINS 36-44% at bfloat8_b 1088B pages. B8 trid = NULL (+5.5ns/txn surcharge > barrier it hides). Root cause recorded: reader/writer are at the per-core NoC ceiling (~29ns per 2KB page), not RISC-issue-bound as the op-level zones suggested.

fused_scale: EVERY fused form is slower than the two-mul baseline. focus per-pass (112 tiles, 20 iters, 1 core, L1-resident): baseline 6641 ns (59.3 ns/tile) | fused_rmsfull 10448 (1.57x slower) | raw_llk same 10368 (so it is NOT chain overhead) | fused_gammafull 13523 | fused_inchain 17262 | fused_sfpu 65633 (SFPU mul ~586 ns/tile) | baseline_reversed 6633 (flat). MECHANISM: no_gamma control = 1 mul = 29.3 ns/tile, baseline 2 muls + full cb_normed L1 round trip = 29.6 ns/mul-tile -> the L1 round trip is FREE (pack/unpack are on other TRISCs); DEST-reuse mul costs ~2x a normal mul. L1: fusion frees 227 KB, but baseline_subchunk56 frees 115 KB for 5% and buys the SAME unlocks (IN_BUF_DEPTH 2 on focus, Regime B->A on (1,1,32,5120)).

VERDICT WIN for the SPAN variant (one 544B transaction covering [0,row0-end) instead of the whole 2048B gamma page). focus 43161->41984 (1.028x, 3 runs agree); prefill_1024 117890->94276 (1.250x); prefill_7168 1236010->1031582 (1.198x); focus_g_fp32 1.128x; prefill_1024_bf8b 1.177x; rank3 1.099x; flat on decode_1024/smallest/RM-gamma/RM-input/no_gamma; NO regression anywhere in a 15-shape sweep. FACES (2 txn, 64B) REGRESSES 0.94x on 1-core Regime B - the op is transaction-bound there, not byte-bound. one-packet issue path = NULL. Option 2 (L1 row0 cache + refill) = REGRESSION everywhere. WIN. focus (1,1,32,7168) baseline 44314 ns -> mcast G=32 9386 ns (4.72x), goal 14894 ns beaten by 37%. PCC 0.999983 vs baseline 0.999987. mcast beats unicast-broadcast at every G. Combine cost grows ~linearly in G (1666ns@G14, 2310@G28, 4001@G56) which sets the optimum at G~32. Domain: TILE wins everywhere (1.17x-7.03x) EXCEPT large G on grid-filling shapes (prefill_1024 g16 0.77x, g32 0.31x - active-core-count starvation from rectangle tiling). ROW_MAJOR input regresses once the per-core stick slice narrows (rm_in_1024 g4 0.59x) because the W split cuts the stick transaction size; TILE keeps a whole 2048B tile page per transaction regardless of G.
